rationale: The blind and acceptance lenses failed (subagent interrupted), and the expected review-standards audit wrote no standards-review.json, so the desktop-unchanged diff check, the Figma acceptance criteria and the commit-format, code-quality and security standards were not verified. 22 blocking findings from the edge-case and verification-gap lenses were confirmed in the source (CR-018's desync branch could not be confirmed; no decision_needed); the main ones are chat state lost when the window crosses 1024px, card tables losing sorting and select-all, and desktop tours auto-starting on mobile. 1 deferred to code-review-deferred.md (a pre-existing valtio subscribe in the render body of Sidebar.tsx that leaks a listener on every render); 2 dismissed as unreachable (the card-mode customRender index argument and falsy row ids).

findings.title: Kata window size not recomputed on resize
findings.problem: windowWidth (line 39) now comes from window.innerWidth, but nothing re-renders the window on resize or rotation, and the saved store.position is never re-clamped. The Draggable bounds (lines 53-58, 120) only apply during a drag. After a phone rotates from landscape to portrait the window keeps its 500px width, and after a tablet rotation it can end up partly off-screen.
findings.impact: After rotation on phones and tablets, the kata window overflows the viewport. Its header controls (restore, collapse, close) can stay out of view until a drag triggers a re-render. The un-clamped position predates this change, but the kata window is part of this change's mobile/tablet adaptation.
findings.recommendation: Re-render on viewport resize (a resize listener or a viewport-size hook), recompute the width and bounds when it fires, and clamp store.position.x/y into the new bounds.

findings.title: Kata window width clamp untested
findings.problem: The new clamp Math.min(store.isCollapsed ? 300 : 500, window.innerWidth - 16) has no test. The only tests that reference FloatingKataWindow (src/__tests__/App.test.tsx:86, src/pages/assistants/__tests__/NewAssistantPage.integration.test.tsx:29) mock it to null.
findings.impact: If the clamp regresses, the 500px window and its drag bounds (right: window.innerWidth - windowWidth, which is negative on a 375px screen) extend past the edge of a phone, and no test fails.
findings.recommendation: Add a FloatingKataWindow test with an active kata: at window.innerWidth = 375 expect a 359px-wide window, and at 1280 expect 500px.

findings.title: Kata window height overflows short viewports
findings.problem: windowHeight is still a fixed 650 (maxHeight 650px, content max-h-[590px] at line 184) whatever window.innerHeight is, so bounds.bottom = innerHeight - 650 goes negative on short screens. Only the width was made viewport-aware.
findings.impact: On phones in landscape, and on small phones in portrait once the browser chrome is taken off, the expanded kata window is taller than the viewport. The end of the step content and its step navigation sit below the screen, and neither scrolling nor dragging reaches them. The height predates this change, but the kata window is part of its mobile adaptation.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the height the same way as the width, e.g. const windowHeight = Math.min(store.isCollapsed ? 60 : 650, window.innerHeight - 16), and derive the content max-height from it instead of the fixed 590px.

findings.title: MobileTopBar has no tests
findings.problem: The new MobileTopBar closes both overlays on any navigation except a query-only change (lines 92-99) and closes them on unmount (102-108). It takes the section label from the first path segment, falling back to the route title (110-115). No test references MobileTopBar, and the global matchMedia stub (src/setupTests.tsx:99) keeps isMobileLayout false, so the App test never renders it.
findings.impact: Losing the query-only guard would close the chat list or filter drawer on every filter change made inside it. Losing the navigation effect would leave the menu open over the next page, and an off-by-one in pathname.split('/') would mislabel every section. No test would catch any of these.
findings.recommendation: Add a MobileTopBar test in a MemoryRouter. Open the sidebar through the store, navigate, and expect mobileNavigationOpen and mobileSidebarOpen to be false. Change only the search string and expect mobileSidebarOpen to stay true. Render /assistants/1/edit and expect the switcher's accessible name to contain 'Assistants'.

findings.title: Escape closes mobile overlay with inner popup
findings.problem: useEscapeKey adds a plain window keydown listener with no handler stack and no defaultPrevented check (src/hooks/useEscapeKey.ts:33-50). Navigation (line 65) and Sidebar (src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:75) now register one while their mobile overlay is open. NavigationProfile and Popup register their own, so one Escape press runs all of them.
findings.impact: In the mobile layout (phones or tablets with a keyboard, and desktop windows narrower than 1024px), pressing Escape to close the profile panel, or a dialog opened from a sidebar, also closes the whole navigation menu or sidebar overlay.
findings.recommendation: Make Escape close only the topmost layer. For example, keep a handler stack in useEscapeKey so only the most recently activated handler runs, or have the overlays ignore Escape while a nested popup is open.

findings.title: Mobile navigation menu branch untested
findings.problem: No test exercises Navigation's mobile branch: rendering nothing unless mobileNavigationOpen (line 195), closing on Escape (65) and on a link tap (68-70, 213), and hiding the logo (216). No test references mobileNavigationOpen or useIsMobileLayout, and the global matchMedia stub (src/setupTests.tsx:99) always reports matches:false.
findings.impact: If the null return were inverted or dropped, the fixed z-50 menu would cover every page on phones. If the link or Escape close were lost, the menu would stay open after the user picks a section. Every existing Navigation test would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add Navigation tests with a mobile matchMedia stub: nothing renders while mobileNavigationOpen is false, header#navigation-menu renders when it is true, and a nav-link click or an Escape press leaves appInfoStore.mobileNavigationOpen false.

findings.title: Mobile overlays leave hidden content focusable
findings.problem: The mobile navigation menu (Navigation.tsx:198-214) and the page-sidebar overlay (src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx:80-85) are fixed full-screen layers over the page. Nothing moves focus into them when they open, keeps focus inside them, or makes the covered page content inert.
findings.impact: Keyboard users, including those in desktop windows narrower than 1024px, tab past the last menu or sidebar item into page content hidden under the overlay. Screen-reader users swipe into the same content. In this new UI, focused elements can be completely hidden.
findings.recommendation: While an overlay is open, make the covered content inert (or trap focus in the overlay). Move focus to the overlay's first item when it opens, and return focus to the top-bar toggle when it closes.

findings.title: Sidebar mobile overlay branch untested
findings.problem: Sidebar's mobile branch has no test: registering with the top bar (lines 69-72), closing on Escape (75), staying hidden until mobileSidebarOpen (85) and hiding SidebarToggle (130). No test references registerPageSidebar or mobileSidebarOpen, and the matchMedia stub keeps every Sidebar test on the desktop branch.
findings.impact: If the registration effect is dropped, the top bar's 'Open sidebar' button disappears, because it renders only while pageSidebarCount > 0. The chat list and page filters that live in Sidebar then become unreachable on phones, and the existing Sidebar tests still pass.
findings.recommendation: Add a Sidebar test with a mobile matchMedia stub. After mount, expect appInfoStore.pageSidebarCount to be 1 and the aside to have class 'hidden'. After setMobileSidebarOpen(true), expect it to be visible. After unmount, expect the count to be back to 0.

findings.title: Card layout drops sorting and select-all
findings.problem: In card mode (lines 204-216), TableCardList replaces the <thead>. Its TableColHeader is the only place sortProps and selectionProps are rendered, and TableCardList receives no sort, onSort, isAllSelected or onSelectAllChange. In the mobile layout, card mode applies to every default-variant table with no footer and no custom rows (lines 180-184).
findings.impact: On phones and portrait tablets, the data sources list (src/pages/dataSources/DataSourcesPage.tsx:173-176, default variant, no footer) can no longer be re-sorted. Other sortable tables that meet the card conditions lose sorting too. The admin users table loses its header select-all, including the lazy all-pages selection (src/pages/settings/administration/UsersManagementPage.tsx:147-150, 405-428). Features that worked on mobile before this change are gone.
findings.recommendation: Give card mode its own toolbar with a sort control, plus a select-all checkbox when onSelectAllChange is passed (e.g. {showCards && (sortProps || selectionProps) && <CardListToolbar sort={sortProps} selection={selectionProps} />}). Alternatively, keep the table layout for tables that pass sort/onSort or select-all.

findings.title: Table card layout has no tests
findings.problem: No test renders TableCardList. Every Table test takes the <table> branch because isMobileLayout is false under the global matchMedia stub, and no test references TableCardList.
findings.impact: A regression in card selection, row-click wiring or id-keyed expansion (for example the admin budget rows in src/pages/settings/administration/UsersManagementPage.tsx:405-420) would ship while TableExpansion.test.tsx and the other Table tests stay green.
findings.recommendation: Add Table tests with a mobile matchMedia stub. Expect li cards instead of a table. Clicking a card calls onSelectRow with that row, and clicking the expand chevron calls onToggleExpand with the row id. The renderExpandedRow output appears once that id is in expandedRowIds.

findings.title: Taps in expanded card toggle selection
findings.problem: Card mode renders the expanded content (lines 128-132) inside the <li> whose onClick is Table's handleRowClick (line 94). That handler toggles selection for any click that is not on a button, link or input. In table mode the expansion is a separate <tr> with no click handler, so this behaviour is new.
findings.impact: The admin users table is both selectable and expandable for budget management (src/pages/settings/administration/UsersManagementPage.tsx:405-420). On mobile, tapping text or empty space inside an expanded budget panel selects or deselects that user, and the selection feeds the bulk-action bar.
findings.recommendation:
Stop click propagation from the expanded area, e.g.
e.stopPropagation()}>{renderExpandedRow?.(item)}
, to match the table layout.

findings.title: Desktop onboarding tour auto-starts on mobile
findings.problem: AutoPopupManager is mounted on every layout (src/App.tsx:91). It starts the navigation-introduction tour for first-time SSO users (lines 71-72) and offers first-visit page tours (lines 96-103) without checking the layout. Yet this change hides HelpPanel on mobile because its tours target the desktop layout (src/App.tsx:94-96), and it stops rendering the logo and the closed menu that those steps target (Navigation.tsx:195, 216). The Help page's tour cards are a separate entry point, covered by CR-020.
findings.impact: A first-time SSO user whose first visit is on a phone, tablet or narrow window gets the desktop navigation tour. Its [data-onboarding=navigation-menu] and navigation-logo targets are missing, so OnboardingTooltip shows fallback tooltips that point at nothing, and the steps that toggle navigationExpanded cannot open the mobile menu. The tour can be skipped, but it is broken on the user's first visit.
findings.recommendation: While useIsMobileLayout() is true, skip the navigation-introduction auto-start and the first-visit page-tour popup, leaving the flow pending for a desktop-width session. Add an AutoPopupManager test with a mobile matchMedia stub that asserts no onboarding session becomes active.

findings.title: Mobile layout media query never tested
findings.problem: useIsMobileLayout has no test. It wraps window.matchMedia(MOBILE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY), defined as 'not all and (min-width: 1024px)' in src/constants/mobileLayout.ts:21, in useSyncExternalStore. The global stub at src/setupTests.tsx:99 answers matches:false for every query and never fires 'change', and no test references useIsMobileLayout or MOBILE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY.
findings.impact: This hook switches the whole shell (src/App.tsx:52, 82-83, 96) and drives every isMobileLayout branch in Navigation, Sidebar, Table and ChatPage. If 'not all and' is dropped, desktops get the mobile top bar and phones get the desktop rail. If the change subscription breaks, a rotated tablet never switches layout. Every suite would still pass, so no automated check guards the requirement that desktop stays unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Add a query-aware matchMedia test helper that evaluates min-width/max-width against a set viewport width. Add a useIsMobileLayout test: true at 375px, false at 1280px, and a re-render with the new value after the registered 'change' listener fires. Reuse the helper in the component tests.

findings.title: useSidebarOffsetClass mobile branch untested
findings.problem: useSidebarOffsetClass now returns 'left-0' in the mobile layout (line 48). src/hooks/__tests__/useSidebarOffsetClass.test.ts never references useIsMobileLayout, matchMedia or 'left-0' and asserts only the desktop offsets.
findings.impact: If the mobile branch is lost, the fixed pagination bar (src/components/Table/Table.tsx:312-319, and the list pages that use the hook) gets a navbar-plus-sidebar left offset on phones. Pagination then moves off a 375px screen while every existing assertion passes.
findings.recommendation: Add a case that stubs matchMedia to match MOBILE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY, sets sidebarExpanded to true and expects 'left-0'.

findings.title: Mobile chat config overlay untested
findings.problem: No test exercises the mobile configuration overlay (lines 207-213, hidden unless isConfigVisible) or its new close button (src/pages/chat/components/ChatConfiguration/ChatConfiguration.tsx:64-72, which calls closeConfig). No test mentions 'Close configuration', and the global matchMedia stub keeps the chat tests on the desktop layout.
findings.impact: On phones the overlay covers the chat header's Configuration toggle. If the close button or the hidden condition breaks, the configuration covers the conversation with no way to close it from the page, and no chat test fails.
findings.recommendation: Add a ChatConfiguration test with a mobile matchMedia stub and isConfigVisible true that clicks the 'Close configuration' button and expects closeConfig to be called. Add a ChatPage mobile test that expects the configuration wrapper to have class 'hidden' while isConfigVisible is false.

findings.title: Config overlay stays over newly picked chat
findings.problem: In the mobile layout, the configuration overlay (z-40, lines 207-213) stays open while the chat-list overlay (z-50) opens above it. Picking a chat navigates away, but MobileTopBar closes only the navigation and sidebar overlays (src/components/Navigation/MobileTopBar.tsx:92-99). useChatConfiguration closes the configuration on chat change only for workflow chats (src/pages/chat/hooks/useChatConfiguration.tsx:177-188).
findings.impact: When a phone user picks a chat from the list, the full-screen configuration stays on top of it. The user sees the configuration instead of the conversation they picked until they close it.
findings.recommendation: Close the configuration overlay when the chat changes in the mobile layout, e.g. useEffect(() => { if (isMobileLayout) chatConfiguration.closeConfig() }, [currentChat?.id]). If keeping it open across chats on mobile is intended, confirm that with product; nothing in the reviewed inputs says so.

findings.title: Layout flip remounts chat, drops attachments
findings.problem: ChatPage renders {isMobileLayout ? mobileLayout : desktopLayout} (line 265). These are two different element trees, so crossing 1024px unmounts one and mounts the other. ChatPrompt keeps attached files in local state (src/pages/chat/components/ChatPrompt/ChatPrompt.tsx:122, useState<FileMetadata[]>), and ChatSidebar, ChatConfiguration and ChatHistory are remounted along with it.
findings.impact: Rotating a tablet across 1024px (most iPads going from portrait to landscape), or resizing a desktop window across it, silently drops the files attached to an unsent prompt. The rest of the page's local chat state goes with them, so the user can send the message without the files. This change introduced it: before, a resize only reflowed the same tree.
findings.recommendation: Keep a single tree and switch the layout with classes and props, or move prompt attachments (and any other state that must survive) into chatsStore so a remount keeps them.

findings.title: Config panel desyncs after layout switch
findings.problem: The sync effect (lines 49-58) runs only when isConfigVisible changes, and it reads panelRef.current. If the configuration was opened in the mobile overlay and the viewport then widens past 1024px, the desktop chat-config Panel mounts with defaultSize={0} (src/pages/chat/ChatPage.tsx:244-254) and the effect does not run again.
findings.impact: One outcome is that the panel stays collapsed while isConfigVisible is true: the header shows it as open and the first toggle does nothing visible. The other is that, if the library reports the 0px mount size to onResize (lines 38-47), the configuration is force-closed on rotation. Which one happens could not be confirmed: it depends on whether react-resizable-panels calls onResize on mount.
findings.recommendation: Run the sync again when the desktop Panel mounts (add isMobileLayout to the effect deps or pass it in), or derive defaultSize from isConfigVisible (isConfigVisible ? CHAT_CONFIG_DEFAULT_WIDTH : 0).

findings.title: Chat sidebar panel desyncs after layout switch
findings.problem: The sync effect (lines 126-138) runs only when sidebarExpanded changes. After a switch from mobile to desktop, the desktop chat-sidebar-panel mounts expanded at defaultSize={initialWidth} (src/pages/chat/ChatPage.tsx:219-229) and the effect does not run again. handleResize ignores resizes made without a pressed pointer (line 104), so a collapsed value in the store is never applied.
findings.impact: Suppose a user collapsed the chat sidebar on desktop, and their window or tablet then went below 1024px and back. They see the sidebar expanded while the store still says collapsed, and their first toggle does nothing. This is a visible desktop change caused by the new conditional layout.
findings.recommendation: Run the sync again when the desktop Panel mounts (include isMobileLayout in the effect deps), or use defaultSize={sidebarExpanded ? initialWidth : 0}.

findings.title: Help page starts desktop tours on mobile
findings.problem: OnboardingToursSection renders a startable card for every tour without checking the layout (lines 42-55), and Help stays reachable from the mobile navigation menu. This change hides HelpPanel on mobile because its tours target the desktop layout (src/App.tsx:94-96).
findings.impact: A tour started from the Help page on a phone or portrait tablet runs its steps against desktop-only targets that the mobile shell does not render. The tooltips point at nothing, and the tour cannot open the closed mobile menu.
findings.recommendation: In the mobile layout, hide the Interactive Tours section, or disable Start on each OnboardingFlowCard with a note that tours need a wider screen (e.g. if (useIsMobileLayout()) return null).

findings.title: Execution history aside not adapted to mobile
findings.problem: WorkflowExecutions renders its own execution-history <aside>, sized by appInfoStore.sidebarExpanded (w-workflow-exec-sidebar, 308px), and an unconditional SidebarToggle (lines 70-76, 103). It has no mobile branch and never calls registerPageSidebar. Sidebar is different: this change turns it into a top-bar overlay and hides its SidebarToggle on mobile.
findings.impact: On a ~375px phone with sidebarExpanded true, the 308px history aside stays inline next to the execution view. The top bar offers no sidebar button for it, and the desktop SidebarToggle still renders, so the workflow execution page was not adapted for mobile.
findings.recommendation: Build the aside on Sidebar so it becomes a registered overlay, or give it the same mobile branch: MOBILE_OVERLAY_CLASS_NAME, hidden unless mobileSidebarOpen, registerPageSidebar while mounted, and SidebarToggle on desktop only. Add a mobile test for it.

findings.title: Mobile overlay store methods untested
findings.problem: The new appInfoStore methods have no tests (lines 442-461): setMobileNavigationOpen and setMobileSidebarOpen close each other, and registerPageSidebar returns a counted cleanup that closes the drawer when the count reaches zero. No test references registerPageSidebar, pageSidebarCount, mobileSidebarOpen or mobileNavigationOpen.
findings.impact: If the decrement is removed, the top bar keeps an 'Open sidebar' button that opens nothing on pages without a sidebar. If the mutual close is removed, both z-50 overlays can be open at once. No test would catch either.
findings.recommendation: Add appInfo.test.ts cases. After setMobileNavigationOpen(true) then setMobileSidebarOpen(true), mobileNavigationOpen is false, and the reverse holds. Two registerPageSidebar() calls give a count of 2. Running one cleanup keeps mobileSidebarOpen true; running both brings the count to 0 and closes it.
